article.story:
In-form Atlético Madrid overcame energetic Elche 3-2 for a ninth win in 10 LaLiga games.

First-half goals from Alejandro Grimaldo, Lee Kang-in and Julián Álvarez put Atlético in control at Estadio Manuel Martinez Valero.

But Elche, just one place off the bottom of the table, refused to surrender and Martin Neto and Buba Sangaré set up an uncomfortable finish for Diego Simeone's side.

Elche defender Federico Redondo suffered a nightmare start as Atlético struck twice inside seven minutes.

The Argentinian stepped on Grimaldo's foot to concede a fifth-minute penalty.

Grimaldo got up off the turf to convert his sixth goal of the season with ease and Redondo was then robbed by Lee, who strode on to arrow the ball into the corner of Matias Dituro's net.

Dituro denied Alvarez after another Redondo error as Atletico threatened to run away with matters.

But Marc Pubill left his backpass short after 27 minutes and Neto made no mistake to curl past Jan Oblak.

Elche fashioned chances for Fer Niño and Lucas Cepeda, but Atlético restored their two-goal cushion four minutes from the break as Alvarez dispatched a delightful pass from Álex Baena.

The game was back in the balance three minutes after the restart as Sangare's shot took a decisive deflection off Dávid Hancko to wrongfoot Oblak.

The LaLiga strugglers pushed on and Oblak saved from Cepeda moments after he had spilled at the feet of Víctor Chust.

Alvarez almost added to Atlético's advantage, but they held on for another three points ahead of Wednesday's trip to Barcelona.
